import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: user_id, item_id, rating, timestamp
# index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: item_id, movie title, and many other columns
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# We only need 'item_id' and 'movie title' columns from Source 1 for the target
df_source1_reduced = df_source1[['item_id', 'movie title']]

# Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'item_id' to get movie titles for each rating record
# This is an inner join because we want only records with matching movie info
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1_reduced, on='item_id', how='inner')

# Ensure the target schema and types:
# Target schema: ['user_id': int, 'item_id': int, 'rating': int, 'timestamp': int, 'movie title': str]

# Convert columns to correct types explicitly
df_joined['user_id'] = df_joined['user_id'].astype(int)
df_joined['item_id'] = df_joined['item_id'].astype(int)
df_joined['rating'] = df_joined['rating'].astype(int)
df_joined['timestamp'] = df_joined['timestamp'].astype(int)
df_joined['movie title'] = df_joined['movie title'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_joined[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
